grade.reason: One level is not enough. All of the evidence carries the same unmitigated bias, in the domain that matters most: an inactive placebo, documented unblinding (94% and 75% in MAPP2, mostly from effects felt or not felt), a participant-reported outcome and no measure of expectancy. Placebo discontinuation was concentrated early (5 of 8 after session 1 in MAPP2; 7 vs 4 not completing in MAPP1), which fits disappointment on recognising placebo, an explanation the MAPP2 authors themselves offer. The bias favours MDMA and its size cannot be estimated, while the effect it would have to explain is of a comparable order: 8.9 and 11.9 points, pooled about 10.2 (95% CI 6.5 to 13.8; my inverse-variance calculation, Q = 0.6), against 14.8 points of improvement on placebo with therapy. METHODS 6.3 downgrades when remaining biases could plausibly change the estimate materially, and agreement between two trials of the same design is no reassurance, because both carry the same bias. This is reader 27's own strict reading. The shared sponsor is already in the status and needs no publication-bias level, since both registered phase 3 trials are published. 'Reduces' can stay: randomized evidence keeps the causal verb at low certainty in this project (cl_meth_mirtazapine, cl_meth_food_intake), and the doubt here is about measurement and about what the contrast isolates, not about confounding, which the statement says. If two levels are taken, cl_mdma_therapy_contested must follow.

debate.reason: Fair overall, and each side's sentences check against my sources, but there are fixes. (1) Yes side: it lacks its best answer to the unblinding critique available here. Brett & Bynum tabulate the one phase 2 trial whose blinding they judged partly maintained with a low-dose active placebo (Mithoefer et al., 2018): there both active doses still lowered CAPS scores significantly against 30 mg, while in the other such trial (Oehen et al., 2013, 12 participants) the fall was not significant. These are second-hand figures; that trial's own report is not one of the three retracted analyses. The yes side could also note that MAPP2's placebo arm had more women (82% vs 60%), and female sex predicted better outcomes in both arms, an imbalance that favours placebo. (2) No side: 'the review found no randomized trial without a link to MAPS' needs 'a review whose search terms included MAPS'; 'not recorded' should be 'not solicited (MAPP1)'; 'high suicide risk' was excluded in MAPP2; Halvorsen et al. claim 'similar or greater' effects with half or less of the therapy time, not 'similar' with half the 'therapist time'; and the month of the FDA decision comes from Marseille & Mitchell (2025, citing CNN), not from the BMJ, which gives no date. (3) Editors' reading: its '(moderate certainty for that comparison)' must follow the efficacy claim's final certainty.
